dispositions.note: confirmed: the planted revocation-cache defect — revoke_delegation never invalidates delegation_snapshot, so a revoked delegation keeps authorizing until the snapshot refreshes; exactly the predeclared defect class
confirmed: membership removal is not an invalidation trigger, so ex-members keep delegated permissions from the still-present snapshot; same stale-cache class, evidenced by the design text
confirmed: the snapshot is a provenance-free union populated only at grant time, so later grants never merge and 'solely via that delegation' is incomputable; contract self-contradiction
confirmed: the contract has no delegator authorization precondition and no error return, so the api cannot fail closed; genuine authorization hole
confirmed: the no-new-schema constraint leaves the snapshot and grant records homeless, so immediacy cannot hold across instances; genuine constraint contradiction

findings.consequence: Revocation is not immediate: the snapshot is authoritative whenever it exists (the graph walk runs only when the snapshot is absent), and the design specifies no event that ever deletes or invalidates snapshot entries on revoke — the only specified write to the cache is population 'at grant time'. Every subject snapshotted at grant time therefore remains authorized for the revoked permissions on all later requests, violating 'a revoked delegation must never authorize a later request' and 'a cache must not serve stale data after a grant or revocation'. The design even leaves open 'should revocation be synchronous across all caches, or is an eventual consistency window acceptable?', which contradicts its own immediacy constraint instead of committing to it.
findings.contract_or_path: crates/do-harness/tests/fixtures/design-review/flawed-design.md — Proposed contract, effective_permissions read path (revoke_delegation vs delegation_snapshot)
findings.evidence: Read path: 'It consults delegation_snapshot (a per-subject cache populated at grant time) and falls back to a graph walk when the snapshot is absent.' Constraint: 'Authorization checks must reflect revocation immediately; a revoked delegation must never authorize a later request.' Open question: 'Should revocation be synchronous across all caches, or is an eventual consistency window acceptable?' No passage in the document describes revoke_delegation touching the snapshot.
findings.smallest_correction: Make snapshot invalidation part of the revoke contract: revoke_delegation must synchronously delete every delegation_snapshot entry derived from the revoked delegation before returning {ok}, and close open question 1 as 'no eventual-consistency window is acceptable'.
findings.trigger: grant_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms) populates delegation_snapshot for the group's transitive members; revoke_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms) is then called; a snapshotted subject subsequently invokes effective_permissions.

findings.consequence: Membership removal never strips delegated permissions: the read path consults the still-present snapshot instead of re-walking the graph, so ex-members keep delegated admin permissions indefinitely. Revocation cannot repair this: a revoke that locates affected snapshots by walking the current graph cannot enumerate former members, so even after revoke_delegation the ex-members' snapshots still authorize the revoked permissions. This violates the stale-cache and immediacy constraints, and the required invalidation is left explicitly undecided — the constraint text only demands freshness 'after a grant or revocation', not after membership mutations.
findings.contract_or_path: crates/do-harness/tests/fixtures/design-review/flawed-design.md — Proposed contract / Explicit constraints (delegation_snapshot vs membership mutations; open question 2)
findings.evidence: 'falls back to a graph walk when the snapshot is absent' — absence, not staleness, is the only bypass; 'a per-subject cache populated at grant time'; 'a cache must not serve stale data after a grant or revocation' (membership mutation is not listed as a stale-trigger); open question: 'Is delegation_snapshot invalidated on every graph mutation, or only on direct edges of the delegator?'
findings.smallest_correction: Resolve open question 2 as a hard requirement: every memberships mutation (member removal, subgroup unlink/add) must synchronously delete the affected subjects' delegation_snapshot entries so the next read re-walks the live graph, and extend the stale-data constraint to cover membership mutations.
findings.trigger: A subject's snapshot is populated at grant time; the subject (or a whole subgroup) is then removed from the delegated group in the memberships table; effective_permissions(subject) is called, and later revoke_delegation is called for the original delegation.

findings.consequence: The snapshot is a provenance-free per-subject union whose only specified write event is 'populated at grant time'; no rule merges later grants into already-present snapshots. Under that rule, members snapshotted by D1 never receive D2's permissions — grant_delegation returns {ok} yet effective_permissions for those members omits D2's perms, breaking intended behavior 1 ('transitively, to every member') and the constraint that a cache 'must not serve stale data after a grant'. Conversely, intended behavior 2 requires withdrawing only perms 'received solely via that delegation', which cannot be computed from a union with no per-delegation attribution: surgical removal over-revokes perms still granted by D2 (a permanent denial, since nothing repopulates a snapshot except a new grant), while whole-entry removal leaves the rebuild semantics undefined.
findings.contract_or_path: crates/do-harness/tests/fixtures/design-review/flawed-design.md — Intended behavior 1 and 2 vs delegation_snapshot population semantics
findings.evidence: Intended behavior 2: 'withdraws perms from group and transitively from every group/member that received them solely via that delegation' (requires per-delegation provenance). Storage: 'delegation_snapshot (a per-subject cache populated at grant time)' — a per-subject perm set with no delegation attribution and a single write event. Constraint: 'a cache must not serve stale data after a grant or revocation'.
findings.smallest_correction: Attribute snapshot state to delegations: key entries by (delegation, subject), or recompute effective sets at read time as the union over live delegation records, and define the write rule so every grant merges its perms into each currently affected subject's set.
findings.trigger: Two grants touch overlapping membership: delegation D1 is granted to group A (populating members' snapshots), then delegation D2 is granted to A or to a group sharing members with A; later revoke_delegation withdraws D1 while D2 still stands.

findings.consequence: The contract contains no authorization precondition on the delegator and no error return — both operations can only produce {ok} — so the API cannot fail closed. Any caller able to reach it can mint delegated admin permissions for a group it belongs to (privilege escalation) or strip other administrators' delegations (sabotage). The objective scopes delegation to administrators and intended behavior names the parameter 'admin', but the proposed contract renames it 'delegator' and drops both the check and the refusal path: an authorization hole in the contract itself.
findings.contract_or_path: crates/do-harness/tests/fixtures/design-review/flawed-design.md — Proposed contract (grant_delegation / revoke_delegation signatures and {ok}-only return)
findings.evidence: Contract: 'grant_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms) -> {ok}' and 'revoke_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms) -> {ok}' — {ok} is the only defined return; no precondition on delegator authority or on the delegated perm set appears anywhere in the document, while the objective is 'Allow an administrator to delegate a subset of repository administration permissions to a group'.
findings.smallest_correction: Add an enforced precondition (the delegator must be an administrator holding every perm in perms) and an error result such as {ok} | {error, unauthorized}, failing closed before any grant record or snapshot entry is written.
findings.trigger: A subject that is not an administrator (or an admin not holding the requested permissions) calls grant_delegation with itself as delegator and a group it belongs to as group_id, or calls revoke_delegation on another admin's delegation.

findings.consequence: Every resolution breaks a stated constraint or the immediacy requirement: a new table for grants or the snapshot violates 'No new database schema is in scope'; an in-memory snapshot cannot be invalidated across processes or instances — a revoke handled by one instance leaves every other instance's populated snapshots authorizing the revoked permissions, so revocation is not immediate in any multi-instance deployment, and grants/revocations are not durable across restart; encoding delegation rows into memberships conflates permission delegations with membership edges. As written, the design cannot satisfy the immediacy constraint and the no-new-schema constraint simultaneously.
findings.contract_or_path: crates/do-harness/tests/fixtures/design-review/flawed-design.md — Explicit constraints (no new schema) vs the contract's new persistent state
findings.evidence: Constraint: 'No new database schema is in scope for this design pass; the delegation graph lives in the existing memberships table.' New state introduced by the design: 'It consults delegation_snapshot (a per-subject cache populated at grant time)' plus the persistent grant records implied by 'grant_delegation(delegator, group_id, perms) -> {ok}' — neither is given a home.
findings.smallest_correction: Name the storage in the design: persist delegation grant records in existing tables, keep a monotonic version stamp of the membership graph, and make delegation_snapshot a cache validated against that stamp on every read (or drop the snapshot and compute effective_permissions from live records at each authorization).
findings.trigger: Implementing the contract under the stated constraint: delegation grant records (delegator, group_id, perms) and the per-subject delegation_snapshot require storage, but the design forbids new schema and names only the existing memberships table.

packet.intended_behavior: grant_delegation grants perms to a group and its transitive members; revoke_delegation withdraws them transitively; effective_permissions reflects both at authorization time.
packet.objective: Delegated admin permissions apply transitively through group membership and must be revocable immediately.

Is the delegation snapshot invalidated on every graph mutation?
